value.rationale: The strip model is a natural infinite periodic graph, where sampling only one transverse rail reduces spatial sensor density by a factor m. It precisely identifies otherwise invisible transverse modes, the minimal temporal horizon, the full-signal uniform frame, and a unique minimax information-volume delay. The unavoidable longitudinal high-frequency penalty forces a finite optimal interval even at two rails (unlike the unshifted finite-path problem), and the continuum constant plus first m^{-1} correction quantify temporal design at large strip width. These features are motivated independently of the computational examples and are not a tautological one-parameter reparametrization.
